items.stem: Why does a chatbot need a 'fallback' response?

options.text: So it can reply politely when it does not understand what the user typed
options.rationale: Correct: a fallback handles inputs the bot cannot match.

options.text: So it can answer every possible question perfectly
options.rationale: A fallback is for when it cannot match, not perfect answers.

options.text: So it never has to reply at all
options.rationale: A fallback is a reply for unknown input.

options.text: So it can ignore the user
options.rationale: A fallback politely responds rather than ignoring.

items.explanation: Correct: a fallback handles inputs the bot cannot match.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO are good steps when planning a chatbot? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Choosing a clear purpose for the bot
options.rationale: Correct: a clear purpose keeps the bot focused.

options.text: Listing the things users are likely to say
options.rationale: Correct: anticipating inputs helps design intents.

options.text: Promising it can answer any question in the world
options.rationale: No bot can handle everything; scope should be realistic.

options.text: Hiding what the bot is for from everyone
options.rationale: Users should know the bot's purpose to use it well.

items.explanation: Correct: a clear purpose keeps the bot focused.

items.stem: Several users type 'hi', 'hello' and 'hey'. How should your chatbot handle these?

options.text: Group them into one greeting intent that triggers the same friendly reply
options.rationale: Correct: similar phrases map to one intent with one response.

options.text: Make a totally separate program for each word
options.rationale: Grouping them into one intent is far simpler.

options.text: Only respond to the exact word 'hi'
options.rationale: An intent should cover similar phrasings.
Greetings should get a friendly reply.

items.explanation: Correct: similar phrases map to one intent with one response.
